description: Aquifer depletion and drought intensify conflict between agriculture cities ecosystems and households.
Extreme weather market disruption and weak safety nets create acute food insecurity.
Extraction pollution and habitat loss weaken water food biodiversity and health.
Speculation land acquisition and weak tenure displace communities and undermine stewardship.
Short-term yield gains undermine long-term productive capacity and water retention.
Technology improves monitoring while increasing platform dependence and unequal access.
Watershed restoration fails when upstream downstream institutions and rights are misaligned.
Regenerative strategy fails if finance rights institutions and monitoring are weak.
